transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], The Drowned Priest [T-04].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the plank walkways of Hollowmoot, and the quarantine bell has not stopped its tired, wet clang since noon. Lanterns gutter under sagging eaves as the crowd in the market square press close around a woman soaked to the bone, her shawl plastered to her shoulders, mud to her knees from wading the last stretch of causeway. She catches sight of you—strangers, capable-looking, still dry enough to have somewhere better to be—and shoves through the press of bodies to grab at sleeves and coat-hems. "My boy," she says, voice cracking, "he heard the singing from the belltower. Saint Orrin's. He's not right anymore, I know he's not, but he's still mine. Please. The water's rising, it'll take the ford by morning tide, and after that—" She doesn't finish. Behind her, someone mutters the word "hive-touched" like a curse, and a Warden at the watchtower rail is already watching the four of you a little too closely.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Your boy's still yours, no matter what took him—I've seen enough good people twisted by this blight to know the difference between corruption and the soul underneath. We'll help you find him, I promise.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde reaches out and steadies the soaked woman with a firm hand on her shoulder, meeting her eyes with the quiet certainty of someone who knows what it means to be cast out. She can feel the Warden's gaze burning into her back, but she doesn't look away from Tessa's face. Some things are worth the risk of being seen.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Your boy heard singing from the belltower—that's not madness, that's the hive marking one of its own. We have until dawn tide swallows the ford. Tell me everything about him, *now*.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous shoulders through the market throng toward the woman, rain streaming off his cloak like scripture. He reads the downpour in real time—the water is rising with *purpose*, speaking in tongues only he can decipher. His eyes lock onto Tessa, and he plants himself squarely before her, ignoring the Warden's weight of attention at the rail. The drowned dead cling to him always; they always *know* when a soul is slipping away.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I know what "not right" means, and I know you're not cursed for loving him anyway. Tell me quickly—what's your boy's name, and when did he hear the singing?

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen gently but firmly takes Tessa's shoulders, meeting her eyes with the steady confidence of someone who has faced the hive before and lived. She doesn't flinch at the word "hive-touched"—her whole life has been shaped by the first outbreak—and she tilts her body slightly to shield the conversation from the Warden's gaze, drawing Tessa close like someone bringing bad news to the kitchen table. Her voice is low, practical, but not cold: the voice of someone who has learned when hope is possible and when it isn't.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I know that look—I wore the grey too. We'll find your boy before the water takes the ford.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire moves through the press of bodies with the steady authority of someone trained to command, stepping into Tessa's reach. She meets the soaked woman's eyes without flinching, even as she feels the Warden's gaze from the watchtower rake across her back. Her jaw sets, and she puts a calloused hand on Tessa's shoulder—a grip that says this isn't negotiable. She'll hold this line, whether the wardens like it or not.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Tessa, listen to me—I'm known here, and that Warden knows my face. Stay close to the others and don't panic. Let me handle this.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Notice: dice - - - 0, invoking Fortune-Teller Who Reads the Rain, Sole Survivor of the Wreck [AL-HC] → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous doesn't wait for an invitation. He plants himself in front of Tessa and reads the rain the way other men read a ledger—the slant of it, the color of the runoff sluicing off the eaves, the particular urgency in how it's falling. "The ford holds till first light, maybe less," he says, flat and certain. "After that it's gone till low tide finds it again, and low tide won't come soon enough to matter." Tessa's breath catches; she gives them the boy's name—Corin—and says he slipped out three nights back, drawn toward the belltower like a man walking in his sleep. But Morwen's attempt to keep this quiet fails her: the Warden at the tower rail has already placed her face, and there's no unseeing a name like hers in a crowd this size. "That's the Exorcist," someone hisses, and heads turn. The Warden starts down the ladder toward the square, hand resting meaningfully on the truncheon at his belt, and the quarantine bell gives one more tired clang as if in answer.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Warden, you see what we see—the blight, the water, the time bleeding away. We're not spreading sickness. We're here to find the boy before he's lost entirely, and before the ford drowns him with us.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward to meet the Warden as he descends, placing herself calmly between him and the rest of the group. Her hands are open, her posture unthreatening but steady—the stance of someone who has faced down her own fears and knows how to meet another person's with clarity. She reads the weight on his shoulders: duty, fear, exhaustion in equal measure. She'll speak to that.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Get out of our way, Warden. That boy's still salvageable, and the flood won't wait for your authority.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps directly into the Warden's path, shoulders squared against the downpour, and the drowned dead press close against his shadow—the Warden will feel it if he's got any sense. His eyes are hollow and certain, the eyes of a man who has already looked into the dark beneath the flood and come back marked. He reaches back for Tessa's arm and starts moving through the crowd toward the belltower, not running, not breaking stride. Just walking. Like a man certain that no Causeway Warden will dare stop him.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Warden, I know what you're trying to protect—and so am I. That boy needs an exorcist, not torches. Give me till dawn tide. You know my work here.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward to meet the Warden before he can close the distance to Tessa, her shoulders squared and her eyes steady. She doesn't defer or retreat, but her voice carries respect—she knows he's trying to protect the city same as she is. She invokes her work as a known exorcist, her long connection to Hollowmoot's pilgrim band, and the simple truth that a boy hive-touched needs an exorcist far more than he needs a pyre. She's not begging permission; she's establishing why she belongs here and why this work matters.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I've still got business with this woman, Warden. Stand down.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire moves with trained efficiency, positioning herself directly between the descending Warden and Tessa. She mirrors his stance, hand resting on her belt, meeting his eyes with the quiet certainty of someone who knows exactly what it means to wear grey—and what it means to be cast out. She hasn't forgotten how to hold a line, disgraced or not.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: You want to test me, grey coat? I still remember the drills. I still remember how to hold.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — overcome with Empathy: dice - - 0 -, invoking Exiled Cook of the Night-Barge Who Hears Everything [YS-HC] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Rapport: dice - 0 - +, invoking Exorcist Who Doubts the Hive Has Souls [MO-HC] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Provoke: dice + - 0 +, invoking Disgraced Warden Who Still Holds the Line on Wick Lane [MI-HC] → Superb (+5) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The Warden's boots hit the last rung and stop. Ysolde's steady voice cuts through the rain—not pleading, just true, reading the exhaustion under his grey coat—and something in his shoulders loosens half a step. Morwen doesn't retreat either; she names herself, and the crowd murmurs it back to him: the Exorcist, the one who walked into the Drowned Temple once already and came out whole. Mire finishes it, planting herself boot-to-boot with him like she's still got a badge to back the stance, and for a long, rain-hammered moment the Warden just looks at the four of them—cast-outs, exiles, a fortune-teller with dead men's eyes—and decides they're not worth the paperwork tonight. "Ford's gone by first light," he says at last, stepping back. "Whatever you're doing, do it fast, and don't let me hear the bell ring for you." Aldous is already twenty feet gone, Tessa's arm in his, walking toward the causeway like the flood itself is clearing a path for him. The others fall in behind, Hollowmoot's suspicious eyes on their backs, the quarantine bell tolling once more into the dark as the town shrinks behind them and the road to Saint Orrin's opens up, drowning, ahead.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The causeway out of Hollowmoot is already ankle-deep and climbing, plank bridges groaning under black water that wasn't there an hour ago. Tessa stumbles along behind you, gasping Corin's name like a prayer, while somewhere ahead — carried wrong-way on the wind, threading under the rain — comes a low, wet chorus of voices in unison, not quite singing, not quite speaking. Half-submerged shrines lean drunkenly out of the flood on either side, and near one of them a huddle of grey, sodden figures kneel in the rising water, unmoving, faces turned toward the sound. They haven't seen you yet. The belltower of Saint Orrin's rises distant and black through the murk, and the water is climbing a finger's width with every breath you take.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Keep close, keep low, don't speak. We move like we're not here.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde raises a fist to signal the others, her eyes fixed on the kneeling figures ahead. She crouches low in the black water and takes Tessa's arm, guiding her firmly but gently away from the shrines. Moving slowly, deliberately, she picks a path through the deeper water along the causeway's edge—where the darkness pools thickest and the sound of their footsteps will be swallowed by the rain. Her body stays between Tessa and the acolytes, shielding her as they slip past like ghosts through the flood.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Don't meet their eyes. The priest's singing has their full attention—they're drinking it like drowning men drink water. We move now, quiet and fast, and they won't know we passed.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous plants his feet and reads the rain like scripture. The drowned dead clustered at his shadow whisper secrets the water has been keeping—the priest's hold runs deep through those figures, binds them to the tower's chorus, pulls them toward something that hasn't fully surfaced yet. He reads the slant of the flood, the exact angle of their kneeling bodies turned away from the causeway, and understands: there's a window. A brief one. The priest's reach is stretched thin across too many souls at once.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Hold. Those are his acolytes, and that chorus is his song calling to Corin. We need to understand what we're walking into before the water traps us between his work and the rising tide.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen raises a hand to halt the group, her eyes fixed on the kneeling figures in the water ahead. The wet chorus—neither singing nor speaking—carries the particular weight of the hive's influence that only an exorcist trained in the Order's care recognizes. She listens intently, drawing on years of knowledge earned in the wreckage of the first outbreak. This is the Drowned Priest's work; she's certain of it. The pattern of it is written in every tone.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Stay close. I'm reading what's ahead before we move into it.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire immediately shifts into position at the group's vanguard, moving with practiced militia discipline through the rising water. Eyes sharp despite the murk and rain, she scans the kneeling figures ahead, reading their stillness, their direction, the pattern of that wet chorus on the wind. Her shoulders set into the stance of someone who's spent years holding a line, and she signals the others to match her pace and stay ready.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ysolde reads the dark water and finds the deepest channel where sound drowns to nothing, drawing Tessa along in her wake like they were never here at all. Aldous watches the acolytes' hunched shoulders and realizes the priest's grip on them is stretched thin tonight — spread too wide across too many kneeling souls — and he marks exactly when their attention will slacken. Morwen listens to the wrong-way chorus and hears it for what it is: not a hymn but a summons, the Drowned Priest's voice pulling the hive-touched toward the belltower note by note, and now she could name the pattern to anyone who asked. Mire holds the vanguard, matching the group's pace to the rhythm Aldous found, and not one grey-robed head turns as the party slips past the shrine, boots silent under the rain's own noise. By the time the kneeling figures stir again, the causeway behind is already vanishing under black water, and ahead — closer now, wet stone rising sheer from the flood — stands Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple, its belltower leaning black against the storm, the chorus swelling louder with every step toward the doors.

ambiguities.section: Rolls / opposition ("Named NPCs roll 4dF + their rating as active opposition")
ambiguities.issue: The Warden was introduced as a named NPC and the GM attempted to use him as active opposition three separate times (events tied to 12–19), but he had no established rating, so the engine refused each attempt. The rules do not say what opposition mode applies to a named NPC who has no defined rating.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table fell back to passive ladder opposition (Average +1, +1 per opposing table aspect) for all three rolls against the Warden (events 17, 18, 19) instead of rolling 4dF for him.

ambiguities.section: Compels ("the GM may offer a compel on any player aspect or trouble")
ambiguities.issue: Both compels in the log (event 10 'Too Famous to Hide', event 16 'Vengeance Over Sense') are logged with the affected player as the 'actor' of the Compel action rather than the GM, leaving it unclear whether these were GM-offered compels merely logged under the target's name, or player-suggested self-compels.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Both were processed as ordinary accepted compels (+1 fate point to the affected player, complication introduced), regardless of who nominally initiated them.

ambiguities.section: Aspects and invokes ("Each aspect once per roll")
ambiguities.issue: Event 11's tags_invoked field lists what could be read as two aspect names separated by a comma ('Fortune-Teller Who Reads the Rain, Sole Survivor of the Wreck [AL-HC]') but only 1 fate point was spent and only a single +2 was applied, which is only valid if this is one aspect with a comma in its title, not two invoked aspects.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as a single aspect (one invoke, +2, 1 fp), consistent with the math shown (total +3 = dice -3 + skill +4 + invoke +2).

ambiguities.section: Rolls (passive opposition vs. named NPC active opposition)
ambiguities.issue: Event 27 (Ysolde vs. 'Kneeling Acolytes of the Drowned Priest') logs opposition as a flat '+1 (NPC + - - 0)'. The rules say passive opposition is Average(+1) +1 per directly-opposing table aspect (max Great +4), OR a named NPC rolls 4dF+rating as active opposition. Here an opposing aspect is explicitly listed (opposing_tags: 'leads fanatical acolytes [T-04]'), which per the passive formula should push opposition to +2, but the log keeps it at +1. Meanwhile a full 4dF NPC roll ('+ - - 0') is displayed but never added into the opposition total, suggesting an active-NPC roll was rolled but not used. The rules text does not say what to do when a named NPC also has an opposing aspect tag, or how to treat a rolled-but-unused NPC dice string.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table appears to have applied a flat Average(+1) opposition, ignored the opposing aspect's +1 bonus, and disregarded the rolled NPC dice entirely, using only the flat ladder value against Ysolde's total.

ambiguities.section: Aspects and invokes / deck-card tags (target_card, opposing_tags fields)
ambiguities.issue: Events 27, 28 and 30 reference card tags (T-04, T-04, H-03) via opposing_tags/target_card fields, but no corresponding draw event with a draw_id appears anywhere in this scene's log, and the costs/compels/fills list for this scene is empty. The baseline rules provided say nothing about how card tags enter play absent a logged draw, so it cannot be confirmed whether these tags were legitimately in play (e.g., drawn in an earlier, unlogged scene) or improperly reused.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as pre-existing/persistent tags carried over from a prior draw not covered in this excerpt; no cost was charged for their use here.

Free compel 'Vengeance Over Sense' has no draw_id (empty) — improvised compel, not a deck-draw cost, so there is no drawn card whose tags could or should have been used.

friction.text: Three engine refusals for 'active opposition from unknown NPC Warden' show the GM repeatedly tried to roll an NPC that had no defined rating before settling on passive opposition, slowing the scene.

An engine refusal flagged a reported fictional trigger ('the party leaves the road or causeway') as not an unused trigger, suggesting a mismatch between the table's narration and the module's trigger-tracking state during the Warden confrontation.

Four players each declared near-identical roleplay/create-advantage actions to intercept the same Warden (events 12–15) before any rolls resolved, creating redundant declarations and spotlight congestion rather than efficient turn resolution.

All four PCs rolled create-advantage/overcome actions this scene with fp_spent 0 and no aspect invokes recorded, despite each having named aspects and situation aspects (from earlier successes) available — the rules permit but don't require invokes, so this is a pacing/engagement note rather than a violation.

The opposition math shown in event 27 mixes passive-ladder notation with an unused NPC dice roll, making it hard to audit whether the +1 vs. Ysolde's Stealth was calculated correctly (see ambiguity above).

No compels were offered during a scene explicitly built around fanatical acolytes and character troubles (e.g., nothing hooked Aldous's or Morwen's aspects into a compel), which is allowed but represents an unused story lever.
